challengeTypes: identify: What are LATITUDES? (Horizontal lines running east to west on the globe vs Vertical lines running north to south | Lines connecting poles | Lines showing time zones)

sort: Drag each latitude feature to its correct description (Equator = 0 degrees latitude, largest circle | Tropic of Cancer = 23.5 degrees North | Tropic of Capricorn = 23.5 degrees South | Arctic Circle = 66.5 degrees North | Antarctic Circle = 66.5 degrees South | Latitudes = horizontal lines parallel to equator)
identify: What is the PRIME MERIDIAN? (The 0 degrees longitude line passing through Greenwich vs The 0 degrees latitude line | The line connecting tropics | The line dividing north and south)

sort: Drag each longitude feature to its correct description (Prime Meridian = 0 degrees longitude at Greenwich | Longitudes = vertical lines from pole to pole | Longitude = measures east or west of Greenwich | 180 degrees = International Date Line | Longitudes = not parallel, meet at poles | IST = 82.5 degrees East longitude)
identify: What is the geographic GRID? (The network of latitudes and longitudes on the globe vs Only latitude lines | Only longitude lines | A map of India)

sort: Drag each coordinate to its correct location (0,0 = Equator and Prime Meridian | 23.5 N = Tropic of Cancer | 66.5 S = Antarctic Circle | 82.5 E = IST longitude | 180 = International Date Line | 0 latitude = Equator)
identify: How many hours ahead is IST (Indian Standard Time) from GMT? (5 hours 30 minutes vs 12 hours vs 1 hour vs 0 hours)

sort: Drag each temperature zone to its correct description (Torrid zone = near equator, hot, between Tropics | Temperate zone = between tropics and polar circles, moderate | Frigid zone = near poles, very cold | Torrid = receives direct sunlight year-round | Temperate = has seasons | Frigid = has ice and snow most of the year)
extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Latitudes — imaginary horizontal lines running east to west, parallel to the equator. Measured in degrees from 0 (equator) to 90 (poles). Important latitudes: Equator (0 degrees, largest circle, divides Earth into hemispheres), Tropic of Cancer (23.5 degrees N), Tropic of Capricorn (23.5 degrees S), Arctic Circle (66.5 degrees N), Antarctic Circle (66.5 degrees S). (2) Longitudes — imaginary vertical lines running from pole to pole. Measured in degrees from 0 (Prime Meridian at Greenwich) to 180 east and west. Prime Meridian passes through Greenwich, London. Longitudes are NOT parallel — they meet at the poles. International Date Line is near 180 degrees. (3) Geographic grid — the network of latitudes and longitudes on the globe. Any point on Earth can be located by its latitude and longitude coordinates. Example: 0,0 is at the equator and prime meridian. (4) GMT and IST — GMT (Greenwich Mean Time) is the time at Greenwich (0 degrees longitude). IST (Indian Standard Time) is the time at 82.5 degrees East longitude (passing through Allahabad). IST is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of GMT. When it is 12 noon at Greenwich, it is 5:30 PM in India. (5) Temperature zones — Torrid zone: between Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn, hot, receives direct sunlight year-round. Temperate zone: between tropics and polar circles, moderate climate with seasons. Frigid zone: between polar circles and poles, very cold with ice and snow. Misconceptions: 'latitudes and longitudes are the same' (WRONG — latitudes are horizontal lines parallel to equator; longitudes are vertical lines from pole to pole), 'the equator is a longitude' (WRONG — the equator is the 0 degree LATITUDE, the largest circle around Earth), 'longitudes are parallel like latitudes' (WRONG — longitudes meet at the poles and are widest at the equator; they are NOT parallel), 'IST and GMT are the same' (WRONG — IST is 5 hours 30 minutes AHEAD of GMT because India is east of Greenwich), 'the torrid zone is cold' (WRONG — the torrid zone is near the equator and is the HOTTEST zone because it receives direct sunlight year-round).
